newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Union to stand ground on JCI working hours.
newsitem.headline: Union to stand ground on JCI working hours.

text.p: South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Tuesday it would not change its stance on working hours at JCI Ltd sites, calling the mining house's threat to sue the union for libel a diversion.
"The realty of the JCI threat is an attempt to derail the NUM focus from mismanagement and poor planning that is costing thousands of jobs," NUM assistant general Gwede Mantashe said in a statement.
The Star newspaper reported on Tuesday that JCI had threatened legal action after the union accused JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo of reneging on a deal over worker retrenchments.

The report quoted a JCI spokesman who said it was the union who in fact reneged on a deal to delay a bout of compulsory redundancies at the Randfontein Estates Gold Mine Ltd in return for the union's agreement to full calendar operations (FULCO).

NUM's Mantashe said 4,000 workers faced retrenchment at Randfontein and a further 3,000 at JCI's Western Areas Gold Mine. Attempts to use the retrenchments as a bargaining chip to introduce FULCO at JCI mines would fail, he added.
"If the retrenchments are a pressure tactic to force the NUM to accept FULCO, that is a dream that will never materialise," Mantashe said.
"Our view is simple. Continued retrenchments will not impose FULCO on us. If we must be taken to court for that, so be it."
